proposition.claim:
After (4.2), p. 13, the proof writes \[G(u,v)=g_2(u)v^2+g_1(u)v+g_0(u),\qquad
 D(u)=\frac{g_1(u)^2-4g_0(u)g_2(u)}{4g_2(u)}.\] Immediately after (4.3), it asserts that the quotient \(q\) and remainder \(h\) in \(g_1=2g_2q+h\), \(\deg h\leq1\), have integer coefficients. The first paragraph of p. 14 then takes \(v=-q(u)\) when \(D(u)\to+\infty\), obtains \(G(u,v)=-D(u)+O(1)\), and concludes (4.6), unboundedness below on \(\mathbb Z^2\). Division over \(\mathbb Q[u]\) does not justify that integer-point selection.

F>=C B^3 outside shrinking neighborhoods of common real zero directions of tilde F4 and F3.

deg tilde Q2=0 if and only if deg R2=deg Q2=0.
